purpose: How to adapt the syntax. The strings in this register were written for a general web search engine. Engines differ: some ignore site:, some need OR in capitals, some drop quotation marks on long phrases, and professional-profile sites often show only a snippet. If an operator is ignored, move the site name into the query as a plain word, shorten quoted phrases to two or three words, and run one query per name instead of chaining OR. Record every string you run and whether the page itself could be opened, so that 'searched and not found' stays separate from 'not searched'. The three lines below show one query rewritten three ways.
queries: linkedin "Goldman Sachs Asset Management" "Client Solutions Group" London
"Goldman Sachs Asset Management" "Client Solutions Group" London analyst OR associate
